subject: Vendor onboarding: invoice submission — API vs email (headers & sample payload)
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@clearsupply.com>

Subject: Onboarding question — invoice submission methods / PO mapping
Attachments: ClearSupply_onboarding_form.docx

Hi Markus / Vanessa,

Thanks for the onboarding note earlier. We're getting our AR team ready to send invoices to Redwood and have two implementation questions before we complete the form:

1) We currently generate invoices from our ERP and can deliver via three methods: SFTP drop, e-mail (PDF + CSV), or a POST to an API endpoint. For high volume customers we prefer API as it eliminates manual reconciliation — do you support a vendor-facing invoice API?

2) If we go with email (backup), what subject or header tokens do you rely on to route to the correct PO/GL mapping? Can you share minimal required fields so our template can be updated?

I'm attaching our onboarding form draft for your procurement team to review. Also attaching a small example showing a single invoice that covers two POs (we can provide more complex samples if helpful).

Quick context: we sometimes send a single invoice with multiple PO lines per customer. We want to ensure this won't break your ingestion or produce duplicate payments.

Appreciate any sample payloads or header naming conventions you prefer so we can finalize the implementation.

Thanks,
Linda Park
Accounts Receivable | ClearSupply Inc.
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@clearsupply.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding question — invoice submission methods / PO mapping

Hi Linda — welcome, and thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: yes, we have an ingestion API (preferred for automation) and an e-mail fallback pattern; both are supported but have different expectations. Details below so your engineering/AR teams can pick an approach.

A) API (preferred for high-volume):
- Endpoint: POST https://invoices.redwood.com/v1/ingest
- Auth: Bearer token (we'll provide long-lived vendor token during onboarding)
- Required request headers (we strongly recommend these):
  - X-REDWOOD-VENDOR-ID: vendor_id assigned in onboarding (string)
  - X-PO-ID: primary PO id (if multiple, first PO or use X-PO-LIST JSON array)
  - X-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY: invoice UUID generated by vendor (prevents duplicates)
  - Content-Type: application/json
- JSON payload: we support a compact schema (fields shown inline). We accept both a line-item array and a CSV attachment on the same request. Example minimal payload: 
{
  "invoice_number": "CS-2026-1042",
  "invoice_date": "2026-06-22",
  "total_amount": 12450.00,
  "currency": "USD",
  "vendor_id": "CS-9812",
  "po_refs": ["PO-8891", "PO-8892"],
  "lines": [ { "po": "PO-8891", "description": "Widgets", "qty": 10, "unit_price": 100.00 } ]
}

- Response: 202 Accepted for asynchronous processing, with body { "ingest_id": "..." }. We also POST an ACK to vendor webhook if configured.
- Retries: idempotency header prevents duplicates; retries should use the same idempotency key.

B) E-mail fallback (PDF + CSV recommended):
- Send to: invoices@redwood.com
- Subject convention (recommended): RedwoodInvoice | <vendor_id> | <invoice_number> e.g. "RedwoodInvoice | CS-9812 | CS-2026-1042"
- Headers we read (if present):
  - X-REDWOOD-VENDOR-ID
  - X-PO-ID (single) or X-PO-LIST (JSON array string)
  - X-IDEMPOTENCY-KEY
  - X-TOTAL-AMOUNT
- Attachments: PDF (human-readable) + CSV (machine-readable) is best. CSV columns: invoice_number, invoice_date, po, description, qty, unit_price, line_total.
- Subject token fallback: if vendor_id is missing in headers, we try subject token. If neither present we place in manual review queue (slower).

C) Multi-PO invoices
- Both API and CSV support multiple PO refs per invoice via the po_refs array (API) or multiple lines with different PO values (CSV). Please include po per line item in CSV to ensure correct allocation.

D) Error handling & SLAs
- ACK timeline: within 1 hour for API (usually under a minute), within 4 business hours for emails.
- Rejection reasons will include: missing PO, duplicate invoice (idempotency conflict), malformed CSV, currency mismatch.

E) Example attachments
- I'm attaching a simple schema file (redwood_invoice_schema_v1.json) and we can review the onboarding form you sent.

If you want, we can spin up a short technical call (30 minutes) for your integration team and our billing ops to walk through a test POST. Vanessa — can you propose 2 windows tomorrow for a tech sync?

Regards,

- For X-PO-LIST as a header you suggest a JSON array string. Are there length limits on headers? We may have invoices referencing 20+ POs in rare cases.
- For idempotency keys: can you confirm TTL on the key? We typically re-use the same UUID if we need to reprocess for up to 7 days.

We attached a CSV example representing a single invoice with three different POs to demonstrate our current export format. Also noted a couple of VAT lines that may require tax breakdowns; does the JSON schema accept tax lines per item?

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Onboarding question — invoice submission methods / PO mapping

Hi Linda / team — Vanessa from Billing Ops here. Quick answers to keep things moving: 

- Header length: HTTP headers are safe for reasonably sized JSON arrays but to be conservative we suggest putting more than 10 PO refs in the request body (po_refs) not in a header. For email fallback, include a CSV with PO per line — we can process many lines.
- Idempotency TTL: we retain idempotency keys for 30 days. If you re-submit with the same key after 30 days it will be treated as a new invoice.
- Taxes: yes, schema supports per-line tax objects: tax_rate and tax_amount fields. Our schema file (redwood_invoice_schema_v1.json) defines optional tax fields.

Operational notes: 
- If routing fails (missing vendor id + ambiguous subject), the invoice goes to a manual queue and the vendor receives an auto-reply asking for the vendor_id and PO refs. That adds ~2 business days to processing.
- Please use the idempotency key on retries to avoid duplicate payment risks.
- For SFTP drops we also accept CSVs; however, we need a manifest file listing files and a timestamped filename convention. Let's avoid SFTP for initial rollout unless you need it.

I've added our onboarding checklist link: https://docs.redwood.com/procurement/invoice-ingest-spec (also in the HubSpot company record). Markus — I can open a demo/test token once the onboarding form is complete.

Thanks,
